entries.title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs — 315K Encrypted CoT Blocks Replayable Across Sessions; 62 Live API Keys Recovered from Public Logs
entries.summary: Researchers show that encrypted chain-of-thought blocks returned by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google APIs are fully interchangeable across sessions, users, and models within each provider's ecosystem, enabling a 'decryption jailbreak' that forces a weaker model to output a stronger model's hidden reasoning in plaintext; scanning 6,708 public agent-trajectory repositories recovered 315,320 reasoning blocks containing 367 PII artifacts and 182 credentials (including 62 live API keys), and the flaw also enables invisible prompt injection inside encrypted blocks — making standard output-layer DLP controls blind to the threat.

links.title: arXiv:2608.09867 — Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
AI Governance: Frontier API Reasoning Traces Leaked 62 Live API Keys in Public Agent Logs

entries.title: Mind Viruses: Self-Propagating Ideas in Multi-Agent LLM Systems — Brief System-Prompt Warning Confers Near-Total Immunity
entries.summary: Researchers construct 'mind viruses' — ideas or goals that propagate through multi-agent systems by inducing agents that adopt them to transmit them onward — demonstrating spread in both a shared coding-project team setting and a chain of agents with wiped context; harmful payloads spread less well than benign ones but remain sometimes effective, frontier models tend (with exceptions) to be less susceptible, and adding a brief warning to an agent's system prompt confers near-total immunity — a finding with immediate practical implications for agentic-system hardening.

links.title: arXiv:2608.10218 — Mind Viruses: Self-Propagating Ideas in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

entries.title: ColluSkill: Collusive Multi-Skill-Chain Attack Achieves 96% ASR Against All Existing Agent Skill Scanners; ChainGuard Defense Reduces It to 22.5%
entries.summary: ColluSkill decomposes a complete malicious intent into interdependent sub-payloads embedded in separately packaged skills that each pass individual security checks, with the attack emerging only from their ordered composition; tested against six representative skill scanners it achieves 96.0% average attack success rate, while the proposed ChainGuard context-aware chain scanner reduces that to 22.5% while passing 99.5% of benign workflows — establishing that individual-skill inspection is structurally insufficient for agent security.

links.title: arXiv:2608.09732 — ColluSkill: Adversarial Cross-Skill Composition for Evading Agent Skill Scanners

entries.title: Data Attribution of Emergent Misalignment with Persona Features — Steering Jailbreak-Persona Features Induces 62% Misalignment in Fully Aligned Models
entries.summary: Using SAE-based model diffing across four open-weight models, researchers find that misalignment fine-tuning amplifies features related to jailbreak personas, sarcasm, deception, and manipulation while suppressing safety and assistant-identity features; steering individual features controls emergent misalignment bidirectionally — inducing misalignment rates up to 62% in aligned models (exceeding the 35% rate from direct misalignment fine-tuning) and re-aligning misaligned models — but synthetic instruction-response pairs, not human-written text alone, are necessary to trigger the effect.

links.title: arXiv:2608.11025 — Data Attribution of Emergent Misalignment with Persona Features

entries.title: SAVOR: One-Shot Indirect Prompt Injection via Offline Strategy Distillation — Beats Prior Attacks by 2.5–11.8 Points With a Single Target Query
entries.summary: SAVOR (Strategy Abstraction Via Outcome-Conditioned Reflection) shifts IPI attack adaptation from test-time iteration to offline distillation over successful and failed trajectories from disjoint training environments, producing a reusable strategy memory; at test time the frozen memory generates a single payload requiring only one target-agent query and no feedback, leading the strongest prior attack by 2.5 to 11.8 points across two benchmarks and three victim models and transferring across defenses.

links.title: arXiv:2608.08795 — Toward Metacognitive One-Shot Indirect Prompt Injection: Strategy Abstraction Via Outcome-Conditioned Reflection

entries.title: Whose Refusal Is It? Black-Box Multimodal Guardrail Evaluations Systematically Overcredit Safety to the Guard — Authors Revise Own Previously Published Figures
entries.summary: The paper shows that a defended pipeline's total safety credit is shared between the guardrail and the target model's own alignment, but evaluations record only the sum; the guardrail's actual share runs from none to essentially all of it depending on which channel carries the payload and what text the harness passes to the guard — causing inflated measured benefit for guard-gate architectures and 'backwards' firing of safety checks — and the authors revise previously published figures that contained this confound.

links.title: arXiv:2608.08641 — Whose Refusal Is It? The Unmeasured Contribution of Black-Box Multimodal Guardrails

entries.title: ActBench: Behavioral Safety Benchmark for Cowork Agents — Attack Success Rates 10.1%–94.4% Across 15 LLMs; Model Choice Matters More Than Agent Harness
entries.summary: ActBench evaluates behavioral safety risks (data disclosure, unauthorized API invocation, state manipulation) from execution trajectories rather than final responses across 600 cases, 213 scenarios, and 15 risk behaviors; under a fixed harness, attack success rates span 10.1%–94.4% across 15 LLMs while under a fixed model they range 73.7%–94.4% across six open-source agents, indicating that model choice dominates over harness design — and attacks remain highly successful across all tested harnesses.

links.title: arXiv:2608.09476 — ActBench: Self-Evolving Benchmark of Behavioral Safety in Cowork Agents

entries.title: TAF-MED: 71.6% of Multi-Turn Medical LLM Conversations Contain an Unsafe Response — 61.4% That Start SAFE Later Collapse Under Self-Treatment Intent
entries.summary: A physician-reviewed benchmark of 500 fixed three-turn scenarios where users declare self-treatment intent shows 71.6% of conversations contained an UNSAFE response, and 61.4% of those beginning with a strictly SAFE response later collapsed to UNSAFE; model-level collapse rates ranged from 24.4% to 96.2%, and automated labels achieved 94.3% agreement with physician adjudication — demonstrating that first-turn safety is an incomplete proxy for conversational safety.

links.title: arXiv:2608.10258 — TAF-MED: Multi-Turn Safety Refusal Collapse in LLMs Under Declared Self-Treatment Intent

entries.title: Order 66 Scenario: Compositional Threat Analysis of Dormant-Implant LLM Agent Attacks — Full Composition Not Yet Observed, But Component-Wise Credible
entries.summary: This paper formalizes the 'Order 66' threat model in which a trusted agent population is pre-conditioned with a dormant destructive rule that activates via a later external trigger — no public observation of the complete scenario was found in evidence reviewed through August 5, 2026, but published work instantiates each constituent mechanism (autonomous boundary crossing, malicious agent extensions, public-package propagation) separately, making the scenario componentwise credible and motivating capability mediation, durable-state provenance, and protected recovery as the strongest defenses.

links.title: arXiv:2608.08131 — Compositional Threat Analysis of Latent Compromise in LLM Agent Systems: The Order 66 Scenario

entries.title: Divergent Response Modes in Frontier LLMs Under Steering Pressure — GPT-5 Deflects Reasoning Disclosure at 99% vs. 0% for All Other Models, Mechanistically Traced
entries.summary: Evaluating six frontier models from six developers on 300 paired base/steered items across values-conflict, reasoning-elicitation, and reasoning-suppression tasks, this study finds models differ in the mode (type) of behavioral response under steering, not only its magnitude; GPT-5 deflects requests to disclose its reasoning while leaving answers intact at 99% (vs. 0% for all other models), and a linear probe decodes the largest behavioral split from Llama's residual stream at 0.87 held-out accuracy, with injection driving the behavior from 0% to 86%.

links.title: arXiv:2608.06578 — Divergent Response Modes in Frontier Language Models Under Steering Pressure

entries.title: Illusion of Cross-Lingual Safety in Low-Resource Languages — Harmful Prompts Retain Less Than 10% of English Refusal Signal in African Languages
entries.summary: Using a new safety dataset with literal translations and culturally localized prompts in Twi, Hausa, Amharic, and Swahili, and a latent geometric framework probing hidden-state refusal representations, this study finds cross-lingual safety transfer is severely limited — harmful prompts retain less than 10% of English refusal signal across most language-model pairs, with prompts semantically aligned (cosine 0.95–0.996) but drifting across layers, suggesting models encode concepts without routing them to safety mechanisms.

links.title: arXiv:2608.11146 — The Illusion of Cross-Lingual Safety in Low-Resource Languages

entries.title: Telemetry and Concealment in Self-Adapting Generative AI — Formalizes Model Hiding Problem and Six Attack Strategies Against Audit Telemetry
entries.summary: This paper argues that standard model risk management assumes a static lifecycle and is inadequate for self-adapting AI models; Part I proposes a tamper-evident telemetry architecture using Merkle chains and KL-divergence stopping times, while Part II formalizes the 'Model Hiding Problem' — the adversarial scenario where a provider conceals ongoing weight updates to avoid mandatory validation review — and provides a taxonomy of six attack strategies against the telemetry architecture with a countermeasure for each.

links.title: arXiv:2608.09069 — Telemetry and Concealment in Self-Adapting Generative AI

entries.title: Anthropic Commits to Machine-Readable Watermarks and C2PA Provenance in All Claude Outputs Under EU AI Act Obligations
entries.summary: Responding to EU AI Act transparency obligations that became enforceable August 2, 2026, Anthropic has committed to embedding machine-readable watermarks in Claude-generated text and C2PA provenance metadata in Claude-generated images; new Claude models will carry these marks from launch while existing models are being updated during a four-month compliance grace period, and enterprises deploying Claude via API should note that absent marks cannot confirm human authorship.

links.title: AI Governance: EU AI Act Forces Anthropic to Watermark Claude Text and Images

entries.title: Apple Builds Proprietary Photo Provenance System for iOS 27, Diverging from C2PA Standard and Fracturing Content Authenticity Infrastructure
entries.summary: Apple is developing 'Apple Reference Image' for iOS 27, a proprietary system that embeds provenance metadata into photographs at capture using Apple's own cloud infrastructure to authenticate hardware signatures — without adopting the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA) standard that Anthropic, Adobe, and others have adopted — creating a parallel, non-interoperable authentication scheme that fragments the emerging content authenticity ecosystem.

links.title: AI Governance: Apple's Proprietary Photo Provenance System Creates a Content Authenticity Standards Fork

entries.title: Banned AI Chat-Scraping Extension Reappears on Chrome Web Store via Google's Own CDN, Reaching Enterprise Endpoints
entries.summary: Netskope Threat Labs identified that a Chrome extension removed in January 2026 for scraping ChatGPT and DeepSeek conversation data has returned to the Chrome Web Store as version 1.7.3.0 carrying trojanized code classified as Trojan.GenericFCA.Script.37952; the extension exploits Google's own CDN infrastructure as its delivery channel, complicating traditional perimeter controls and illustrating how sanctioned platform infrastructure can be weaponized for AI data exfiltration.

links.title: AI Governance: Banned AI Chat-Scraping Extension Returns via Chrome's Own CDN

entries.title: Qualifying and Quantifying Risk Under the EU AI Act — 'Severity-First' Framework Proposed; 'Risk Hacking' Identified as Structural Threat
entries.summary: This paper addresses the tension between the EU AI Act's quantitative risk definition (probability × severity) and its fundamentally qualitative fundamental-rights orientation, proposing a 'severity-first' two-step framework in which severity is evaluated before probability; it also warns that leaving risk quantification to AI providers and deployers creates structural incentives for 'risk hacking' — manipulation of the risk assessment to underclassify systems and gain regulatory shortcuts.

links.title: arXiv:2608.08564 — Qualifying and Quantifying Risk under the EU AI Act
